notes:
I don't have any notes for you yet, because the research didn't get far enough to read a single source page.

I sent the first batch of requests, for Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Bible Hub and the NET Bible notes on Psalm 18. Each page came back in a format my script didn't expect, so the script stopped before saving or showing any text. After that, the tool wouldn't let me run any more searches or page fetches in this session.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for every point. Since I didn't read any pages, I've left the notes out rather than write them from memory.

If you send the request again, I'll start with these sources:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-18/
  - The Bible Hub commentary pages for Psalm 18:1–25 (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*)
  - preceptaustin.org
  - Studylight
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Spurgeon on spurgeon.org, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus Ligonier, Desiring God and the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org). I'd focus on verses 20–24, where David speaks of being rewarded "according to my righteousness."
- **Other views:**
  - The NET Bible notes on the Hebrew of verses 4–5 ("torrents of chaos," Sheol) and on verse 25
  - Bible Odyssey on the storm-god imagery in verses 7–15
  - Augustine's commentary on this psalm on newadvent.org (his Psalm 17, because he follows a different numbering)
  - Any material on these verses from gotquestions.org about prosperity or word-of-faith teaching
